frequency_question: How often do state high courts strike down contested map challenges during the final weeks before candidate filing or ballot finalization deadlines?
membership_rule: Includes state supreme court final rulings on partisan or racial gerrymandering of congressional/legislative maps where a decision was rendered within 30 days of an election administration deadline. Excludes federal court primary litigation and cases dismissed purely on standing without reaching merits.

cases.name: North Carolina Supreme Court (Harper v. Hall)
Pennsylvania Supreme Court (League of Women Voters v. Commonwealth)
Ohio Supreme Court (League of Women Voters v. Ohio Redistricting Comm.)
New York Court of Appeals (Harkenrider v. Hochul)
Wisconsin Supreme Court (Johnson v. WI Elections Commission)

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major state supreme court interventions on maps under tight pre-election deadlines.
known_gaps: Does not exhaust all minor state court challenges, focusing strictly on high-salience state supreme court rulings on maps under compressed timeframes.
skeleton: State supreme court redistricting invalidations under expedited pre-election dockets, sampling major contested state cycles since 2010.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable expedited high-stakes state high court rulings.
validity_reason: State judicial review patterns for redistricting remain stable until the next decennial census cycle post-2030, though minor shifts in state court compositions apply.
